Good for only heavy, unbreakable (super strong), sealed-by-you items, and super lucky people.

Had a drum that didn't even flinch when we (70kg people) sat on it. They managed to destroy it. Requested a box with super fragile materials to be marked as fragile, they didn't do it (rather marked another smaller as fragile that didn't need it). And yes, they broke things.

Sent 2 packets of power-ish items (chhaatu) inside steel utensil with lid, don't know how, but those packets weren't intact.

Oh and most importantly, they used our utensils before sending.

Yeah, even with broken items, total costing was still less than popular movers. We were only lucky to have the only 2 items that we cannot measure in price (a flat stone & a glass material) delivered intact, despite the box not saying fragile (the packaging was quite good for the 2). Note, couple other items in the carton were broken. So, if you're having way to high trust on your luck, have them.

EDIT: The management is now suggesting me what I should have/carry & what I shouldn't. LoL. And about using our items, this is not to claim they don't have equivalent items, but after our carefully washing & wiping of the materials, after delivery we found utensils sticky at places usually formed after a regular use, and also oil sticking to various parts of the utensils, while we didn't even send any oil anywhere. What should I deduce from it?

I guess the manager would also suggest us to not carry food preparing utensils since there's a lot of bend & deep scratches on them too. What an idiotic reply after damaging so many of the items that were supposed to be strong enough (but the delivery partners were stronger).
